text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday, prepared for Reuters by the Estonian news agency ETA. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Relations with Russia could be improved if personal contacts between prominent figures are used, ex-prime minister Tiit Vaehi said after a eeting with Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov.
- Former agriculture minister Jaan Leetsar and four senior ministry officials gained ownership of apartments in a state-owned block unlawfully, the justice ministry said.
- The modern ferry that the shipping company of Saaremaa island bought recently will start a new era in traffic between the mainland and the islands, the company director said.
- The interior ministry violated the law on the state budget when they bought vehicles with funds allocated for the police department, the chairman of parliament's fiscal commission said.
- Vaehi's meeting with Primakov was co-ordinated with the foreign ministry and the ministry was informed about its results, Foreign Minister Toomas Hendrik Ilves said.
- The government approved directives for forming Estonian reserve troops, planned to be some 26,000 men by 2000, Defence Minister Andrus Oovel said.
- 125 foreign students in Tartu University face expulsion because of unpaid university fees. Students are protesting against increased fees which they have to pay by April 16.
- The situation of people who belong to the large Russian minority in Estonia has improved, OSCE minorities commissioner Max van der Stoel said on a visit to Tallinn.
- Forged tickets for Michael Jackson's concert are circulated in Tallinn, organisers of the event warn the fans.
- Three state-owned casinos, managed by Eesti Loto and an Austrian partner Novo Invest Casino Development, opened their doors in Tallinn and Parnu.
- The government approved plans for privatising Estonian Railways. It will be reorganised into four companies and part of their shares sold, the transport ministry said.
